title: Gudibande Fort
tagline: Bengaluru → Devanahalli → Chikkaballapur → Gudibande. ~95 km, a 17th-century hill fort with 19 rock-cut rainwater tanks.
summary: Gudibande Fort crowns a conical granite hill above a small town and lake in Chikkaballapur district. It was built in the 17th century by the local chieftain Byre Gowda, remembered as a Robin Hood who robbed the rich to help the poor. Around 400 broad stone steps climb through gateways and seven levels of walls past a chain of linked rock ponds to the Rameshwara temple on top. The ride is almost all on smooth NH 44, with a short run on district roads at the end.

segments.note: City exit and the fast airport highway to Devanahalli.
Four-lane highway past the Nandi Hills turn-off to Chikkaballapur.

segments.road: NH 44, then district road to Gudibande
segments.note: More highway north, then a left onto quieter district roads through farmland to Gudibande town and its lake; narrow lanes lead to the foot of the hill.

highlights: 17th-century hill fort of Byre Gowda, the local 'Robin Hood'
19 rock ponds and tanks ('dhones') linked so overflow fed the next, holding ~3 lakh litres
Seven levels of walls, gateways and sentry posts on the way up
Rameshwara (Shiva) temple at the summit, said to hold one of the 108 Jyotirlingas
Views over Gudibande Lake and the plains to Varlakonda

offroad.summary: Paved all the way to the base of the hill; the climb is on foot.
notes: Last stretch is narrow town lanes to the foothill — park near the base
Above the steps there is a short scramble over rock to the top

timings: No formal entry fee or permit reported; at most a nominal local fee
~400 stone steps, ~45 minutes to the top at an easy pace
Leave Bengaluru by ~6–7 am to climb before the heat
Fuel and food are on NH 44 and in Chikkaballapur; carry water for the climb
cautions: Exposed rock near the top is slippery when wet — avoid in heavy rain
Little shade on the hill; carry water and sun cover
Stray dogs reported around the town lanes
